articleTitle: Preface to special issue based on the joint AP/MTT symposium held at university of pretoria on 17 november 1995
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: The Guest Editors are pleased to offer you, the reader, this Special Issue which is based on papers presented at the Joint AP/MTT Symposium held in Pretoria during November 1995. This Symposium was organised by the IEEE's South Africa Section and the SAIEE in terms of the existing cooperation agreement between the IEEE and the SAIEE. A total of 34 papers were presented. Several of these papers were selected for possible publication in a Special Issue, and referred to reviewers in South Africa and abroad to assess their suitability for inclusion.

articleTitle: Full-wave analysis of a longitudinal narrow-wall waveguide slot coupled with an internal e-plane fin
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: This paper describes a full-wave computational electromagnetics model of a longitudinal slot in the narrow wall of rectangular waveguide coupled with an internal thin E-plane fin inside the waveguide. The waveguide wall is assumed to have finite thickness. Appropriate Green functions are used in a method of moments solution of the magnetic current distributions in the waveguide slot, and the electric surface current on the fin. Results obtained with an implementation of the model are verified by comparison to measured results, and illustrate the ability of the E-plane fin to affect the radiation characteristics of the waveguide slot.

articleTitle: Using simulated annealing for extremely nonlinear circuit analysis
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: Analysing a step recovery diode circuit causes problems because of the extreme nonlinearity of the diode currents. This paper shows how simulated annealing can be used successfully as an algorithm to obtain a solution for the waveform balance technique when applied to such a circuit.

articleTitle: Combined numeric and analytic methods for foil winding design
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: A new approach to eddy current analysis in foil windings, using a combination of numerical and closed form analytic solutions, is proposed. The method requires less computing power, is faster than finite-element methods and is more accurate than traditional one-dimensional closed form analytic techniques. The method is applied to a foil winding inductor and its accuracy is compared to a finite element solution of the same problem. The method has been successfully implemented in a CAD program.

articleTitle: AN 18-40 GHz Omni-directional antenna for enhanced elint systems
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: An 18 - 40 GHz omni-directional antenna capable of receiving horizontally and vertically polarised signals was developed and is reported on as an upgrade to many ELINT systems which operate up to 18 GHz only.

articleTitle: Discrete implementation of a nyquist filter
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: Although the necessity for Nyquist filters in radio equipment is well understood, implementing such filters using discrete elements remains difficult. In this regard, several approximations to Nyquist filters have been proposed, mainly focussing on the removal of InterSymbol Interference (ISI). In this correspondence, it is shown how a true Nyquist filter with arbitrary roll-off can be implemented using discrete analogue components. Furthermore, the importance of phase equalization is described mathematically and by simulation. Finally, some filter design tables for raised-cosine and square-root raised cosine filters are presented.

articleTitle: Doubly curved reflector shaped in one plane: Some design considerations
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: Parametric studies are applied to a doubly curved reflector antenna shaped in the elevation plane to firstly examine the far-field elevation pattern ripple as a function of the feed tilt angle. The beam angular peak position as a function of the antenna shaping parameters is then examined

articleTitle: An atmospheric turbulence chamber for optical experiments
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: A turbulence chamber suitable for optical propagation experiments was developed using off-the-shelf components. It attempts to physically simulate atmospheric turbulence under laboratory conditions. A description of the chamber is presented as well as a characterisation of the turbulence. An application example of image degradation/restoration is also given.

articleTitle: Highly linear and low offset n-GaAs hall sensor
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: A novel n-GaAs Hall sensor is investigated. The sensor structure is grown by liquid phase epitaxy on a semi-insulating GaAs substrate. The sensor is characterised by an absolute magnetosensitivity S DL = 1 V/T, nonlinearity not exceeding 0.05 %, and offset voltage not exceeding 20 μV for a magnetic field within the interval [-1.5,1.5] T at room temperature. The influence of the technology and the design on the characteristics of the sensor is investigated.

articleTitle: Wireless in the second anglo boer war 1899-1902
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: The Anglo Boer War of 1899-1902, will be remembered as the last of the gentlemen's wars the war that marked the end of the Victorian era. For military communications however, it commemorates a beginning, for it was during the Boer War that wireless was used for the first time by an army on active service. This paper will discuss the reaction of both Boer and British forces to the invention of wireless telegraphy. The Boers so often described by the British popular press of that time as being solitary uneducated, solemn people who were resistant to change, were eager to obtain “wireless” equipment which they saw as the answer to their military communications problems. The appearance of wireless into British military circles was to prove to be a stormy one, with many years passing before wireless was fully accepted by the British, as the military necessity it is today.

articleTitle: The numerical analysis of planar antennas buried in layered media
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: A moment method formulation for the rigorous numerical analysis of planar antennas buried in layered media is outlined. The formulation is an extension of work done by Rao, Wilton and Glisson on the triangular discretization of the conducting regions, and by Mosig on the Green's functions of multilayered regions. The method has been tested by comparing its predictions with measurements made on an Archimedes spiral antenna embedded between dielectric and absorbing layers. The resulting code has been used for various antenna engineering purposes.

articleTitle: Radiation from microstrip right angle and T-junction discontinuities
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: This paper reports on the field patterns and radiation resistance associated with radiation from microstrip right angle and T-junction discontinuities. The aperture field model is used to investigate the fringing fields with results showing the localised nature of the radiation. Good agreement between the predicted and measured fields is shown and the radiation conductance for the T-junction is shown to be proportional to branch arm width and the conductance of the right angle proportional to the square root of the side arm width.

articleTitle: The cost of load scheduling of a steel plant when operating under RTP
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: Abstract The real time pricing tariff (RTP) or spot pricing as it is also known can be of great value to the supplier [2,3,4] as well as to the end-user of electricity [5,6,7]. Load management options for the consumer have been researched [8,9] extensively and when they are incorporated by a user one of the options is that load switching can be done in order to avoid the peak tariff charges. This can result in losses such as switching losses, losses in production, loss in efficiency and many more [1,10] could occur. These losses that occur when load scheduling is done in response to RTP will be inspected in this paper. As a case study a model of a steel plant will be subjected to this losses that can develop when load scheduling is done.

articleTitle: New proposed structural design and manufacturing tolerances for HF log-periodic dipole arrays
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: Stringent guidelines are usually followed for structural design and manufacturing tolerances of HF log-periodic dipole arrays. When such antennas are manufactured on site, and/or erected in isolated areas with unskilled labour, these tolerances can easily be exceeded. This paper reports on a study which indicates that the accepted tolerance guidelines can be relaxed significantly, without detrimentally affecting the antenna's gain, radiation pattern or input impedance.

articleTitle: Computer Aided Modelling of an Injection-Locked Oscillator for an Active Array
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: The computer aided modelling of an injection locked microwave oscillator, intended for active array applications, is investigated. A simple feedback oscillator is designed and optimised for operation at 8GHz. Frequency and time domain simulations of the free-running oscillator compare well with measurements. The injection locking behaviour is described and measured, but stable and accurate predictions are difficult to achieve. Modelling limitations are discussed in the light of experimental results.

articleTitle: Markov channel models for ds-cdma communications
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: One of the most important parameters of a Direct Sequence Code Division Multiple Access (DS-CDMA) system, is the average bit error rate (BER) as a function of the average signal-to-noise ratio, the number of users in the multiple access environment and the system's processing gain. Due to the complex nature of a DS-CDMA system, simulations to obtain the average error rate are very time consuming, especially when the number of users and the processing gain is large. In this note, we present an alternative method of simulating a DS-CDMA system, based on the Fritchman channel model. Using this method, the simulation time is independent of the number of users and the processing gain of the system. Furthermore, results obtained using the Fritchman model clearly show that the common approximation of the Multiple User Interference (MUI) as a Gaussian noise source is not valid under all circumstances.

articleTitle: AN 18-40 GHz SCAB on’ spiral antenna for enhanced ESM systems
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: Modern ESM systems require frequency coverage up to 40 GHz. This paper describes the development of a small 18 - 40 GHz spiral antenna that can be mounted alongside the antennas of lower frequency ESM systems to extend the bandwidth thereof.

articleTitle: An automatic testing system for electronic party line subscriber cards
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: A computer-based system for undertaking complete functional testing of subscriber cards on the Zimbabwe telephone network is described. The hardware simulates the actions of both the exchange and the subscriber, and is controlled by software through a digital interface to a personal computer. The resulting system has been tested in the production environment, and demonstrated a testing speed increase of about twenty times compared with the manual method previously used.

articleTitle: FDTD analysis and gaussian beam measurement of frequency selective surfaces
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: The analysis of frequency selective surfaces (FSS) using the Finite-Difference Time-Domain (FDTD) technique is reviewed. Results are presented for FDTD predictions and measurements using a free-space Gaussian beam measurement system for both tri-slot and ring FSS flat plate samples. Some practical considerations affecting radome applications are discussed, including Floquet modes, thick dielectric supports (single-sided vs. sandwiched), slot fillings and surface waves. Other computational methods are outlined and some conclusions drawn regarding optimal methods for FSS analysis. Current work in progress on radome applications is outlined.

articleTitle: Adaptive dual carrier phase and frequency kalman estimator for 4D-QPSK
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: This paper investigates a dual carrier phase and frequency correction strategy, specially adopted for application in a Four-Dimensional Quadrature Phase-Shift Keying (4D-QPSK) modem. The modem is intended for asynchronous V/UHF digital land mobile communications, with Time-Division Multiple-Access (TDMA) or Slow Frequency-Hopped Multiple-Access (SFHMA) transmission scenarios. Performance results are presented to illustrate the efficiency of the Dual Carrier Phase Frequency Kalman Estimator (DCPFKE) strategy under typical mobile channel conditions, excluding the effects of multiplath and deep amplitude fades.
